data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The resilience of a decentralized network is a fallacy of 'noise masking'; the large service is more resilient due to its ability to execute global traffic evacuation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The global control plane itself is the source of the failure (the 'Complexity Paradox' from SCR_003).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The speed of traffic evacuation is slower than the propagation speed of the correlated failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"While a decentralized network avoids single-plane config errors, it lacks the global observability and control required to route around failures rapidly. A large service, despite the risk of correlated failure, can implement a 'global kill-switch' or rapid evacuation of traffic from a failing region to a healthy one (ref: SRC_008). The apparent resilience of the decentralized network is merely the result of failures being too fragmented to be noticed as a 'systemic' event until the aggregate loss of utility exceeds that of a single large-scale outage.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
